41	\paragraph{Diminishing returns of $N$-scaling.}
42	Our $N{=}8$ and $N{=}16$ comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:robustness}) characterize the marginal value of additional samples for test-time scaling \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}.
43	For quality estimation, structural signals benefit consistently but sublinearly: SJ $\rho$ improves by $+0.055$ (Qwen SciERC, 3-seed mean) and $+0.032$ (LLaMA CoNLL, 3-seed mean) when doubling from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$, while log-probability is approximately $N$-invariant ($\Delta\rho{\leq}0.021$).
44	Structural signals leverage $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise comparisons (28 pairs at $N{=}8$, 120 at $N{=}16$), but the $\rho$ improvement is far less than proportional, indicating diminishing information per additional comparison.
45	This asymmetry gives structural signals a relative advantage in the compute-constrained regime: at $N{=}8$, SJ already achieves $\rho{=}0.431$ on LLaMA CoNLL (vs.\ logprob $\rho{=}0.307$, $\Delta{=}{+}0.124$), and the gap \textit{widens} at $N{=}16$ ($\Delta{=}{+}0.153$) because structural signals continue to benefit from additional pairwise evidence while logprob does not.
46	For sample selection, additional samples increase the oracle upper bound---more draws raise the probability of a high-quality candidate---but signal-based selection remains flat because the selector's inability to identify the best candidate is a granularity limitation, not a sample size limitation.
47	The practical implication is that $N{=}8$ captures most of the achievable quality estimation benefit; further scaling widens rather than closes the correlation-selection gap absent stronger per-sample selectors.

20	Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} uses KL divergence between a sample's token distribution and the prior to select high-quality outputs, demonstrating that reward-free selection is viable for mathematical reasoning.
21	ReASC \cite{kim2026reasc} adaptively adjusts the number of samples based on estimated difficulty, while \citet{wang2025rankedvoting} replace plurality voting with ranked aggregation, and \citet{oh2025latentsc} perform consistency estimation in latent space rather than output space.

23	All of these methods target reasoning and QA tasks with discrete or near-discrete answer spaces.
24	Our work is, to our knowledge, the first to extend self-consistency to set-valued structured outputs in IE, and the first to identify the correlation-selection gap: strong quality estimation ($\rho{=}0.50$) coexists with selection failure (no gain over greedy on NER).
25	In direct dialogue with \citet{kang2025selfcertainty}, who show that reward-free selection succeeds for reasoning, our results demonstrate that this success does not transfer to structured extraction, where the combinatorial output space and instance-level nature of consistency signals preclude effective per-sample discrimination.

3	\paragraph{Practical recommendations.}
4	Our results suggest different signal choices depending on the deployment scenario.
5	For per-instance quality estimation, entity voting provides the strongest single signal ($\rho{=}0.38$, Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}).
6	When temperature or cross-condition robustness is required, SJ is preferable: its temperature sensitivity is small with bootstrap CIs including zero (Table~\ref{tab:robustness}), and it generalizes beyond entity-level structure to any set-valued output.
7	Under conditional filtering, EM leads on both NER and RE ($\rho{=}0.408$, $0.485$; \S\ref{sec:complexity_robustness}), extending binary-agreement advantages to the within-capability regime; the SJ+Voting ensemble reaches AUROC${=}0.735$ on the full set.
8	For binary accept/reject decisions, logprob is most effective (AUROC${=}0.761$ on CoNLL with LLaMA).
9	For best-of-$N$ selection, greedy decoding is near-optimal on NER; on RE, logprob is the only helpful signal (+2.3~pp, Table~\ref{tab:selection}).

11	\paragraph{Signals discriminate between instances, not within strata.}
12	When instances are stratified by greedy F1, within-stratum correlations approach zero for all signals.

\paragraph{NER: marginal gains only.}
The oracle upper bound (0.776) reveals 13.2~pp of headroom above greedy (0.644), confirming that substantially better candidates exist among the $N$ samples.
Log-probability achieves the best selection (0.650, +0.6~pp over greedy), and SJ marginally exceeds greedy (0.645, +0.1~pp), but both improvements are ${<}$1~pp---capturing less than 5\% of the available oracle headroom.
Voting ($\rho{=}0.379$, the best quality estimator) selects to only 0.634, \textit{below} greedy.
The near-greedy performance of all signals implies that the $N$ samples cluster at a similar quality level: confidence signals can identify which instances are hard but cannot distinguish among near-identical candidates for a given instance.

\paragraph{RE: no signal surpasses greedy.}
On RE, the correlation-selection gap is complete: no signal exceeds greedy (0.404).
Log-probability selects to 0.395 ($-$0.9~pp) and SJ to 0.386 ($-$1.9~pp), despite an oracle gap of 18.1~pp (0.585 vs.\ 0.404) indicating substantial per-instance variance.
Unlike NER, where logprob's per-token evaluation provides marginal selection value, compound entity-then-relation decisions create extraction errors that even per-sample signals cannot diagnose: a sample may have high token-level confidence yet extract the wrong relation arguments.
